# Datasets and reported results in the Tsetlin-machine literature

<!-- Generated by build_catalog.py from papers/*.json - edit those records, not this file. -->

Extracted from the 55 Tsetlin-machine papers in `source_documents/papers/`: **128 datasets**, **3295 reported numbers**.

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `papers/<paper_id>.json` | One record per paper: bibliographic data, TM variant(s), the new feature, datasets (sizes, splits, Booleanization, download link) and every extracted result. **Source of truth.** |
| `datasets.json` | One entry per dataset: metadata, download link, and every paper/TM variant that used it, with the split as that paper reported it. |
| `results.csv` | Flat table of all reported numbers (proposed models and baselines). |

Caveats: numbers are as *reported by the authors* (not reproduced), splits and Booleanization differ between papers, so cross-paper comparisons need care. `download_url_source = well_known` means the paper named the dataset but not a link, and the official public source was filled in. Sizes marked "standard sizes, not stated in paper" in `split_as_reported` were filled from the dataset's standard split. Papers that predate the hard clause-budget cap or use other implementations are not directly comparable to `torchtsetlin` numbers. Ten FHE / privacy background papers in `08_privacy_fhe_tm/` contain no Tsetlin-machine experiments and are not included.

### Using the Tsetlin Machine to Learn Human-Interpretable Rules for High-Accuracy Text Categorization with Medical Applications (2018)

`2018_TM_Human_Interpretable_Rules_Text_Categorization_Medical_Applications_arXiv1809.04547` · arXiv preprint (later published in IEEE Access, vol. 7, 2019) · arXiv:1809.04547 · [code](https://github.com/cair/TextUnderstandingTsetlinMachine)

**TM variants:** Vanilla TM (multi-class)

### The Tsetlin Machine - A Game Theoretic Bandit Driven Approach to Optimal Pattern Recognition with Propositional Logic (2018)

`2018_The_Tsetlin_Machine_Game_Theoretic_Bandit_Driven_Approach_arXiv1804.01508` · arXiv preprint (v15, Jan 2021) · arXiv:1804.01508 · [code](https://github.com/cair/TsetlinMachine)

**TM variants:** Vanilla TM, Multi-class TM  
**New feature (algorithm):** Introduces the Tsetlin Machine: teams of Tsetlin Automata composing conjunctive clauses, trained by Type I/Type II feedback in a game whose Nash equilibria correspond to optimal propositional pattern recognition. Also introduces the multi-class (argmax) TM.  
**Datasets:** `iris`, `uci-digits`, `axis-and-allies`, `noisy-xor`, `mnist`

### The Convolutional Tsetlin Machine (2019)

`2019_The_Convolutional_Tsetlin_Machine_arXiv1905.09688` · arXiv preprint (v5, Dec 2019) · arXiv:1905.09688 · [code](https://github.com/cair/pyTsetlinMachineParallel)

**TM variants:** Convolutional TM, Vanilla TM, Weighted TM  
**New feature (architecture):** Convolutional Tsetlin Machine: each clause acts as a WxW convolution filter evaluated on every patch (augmented with thermometer-coded patch coordinates), output ORed over patches; feedback is given against one randomly chosen matching patch. Also introduces integer clause weighting.  
**Datasets:** `noisy-2d-xor`, `mnist`, `kuzushiji-mnist`, `fashion-mnist`

### The Weighted Tsetlin Machine: Compressed Representations with Weighted Clauses (2019)

`2019_The_Weighted_Tsetlin_Machine_arXiv1911.12607` · arXiv preprint (v4, Jan 2020) · arXiv:1911.12607 · [code](https://github.com/adrianphoulady/weighted-tsetlin-machine-cpp)

**TM variants:** Weighted TM, Vanilla TM  
**New feature (algorithm):** Real-valued clause weights learned jointly with clause composition (multiply by 1+gamma on Type I, divide on Type II), letting one clause replace many. Also a binomial+uniform sampling scheme for Type I feedback that speeds feedback generation ~7x.  
**Datasets:** `mnist`, `imdb`, `connect-4`

### Closed-Form Expressions for Global and Local Interpretation of Tsetlin Machines with Applications to Explaining High-Dimensional Data (2020)

`2020_Closed_Form_Expressions_for_Global_and_Local_Interpretation_arXiv2007.13885` · arXiv preprint · arXiv:2007.13885

**TM variants:** Integer Weighted TM, Regression TM  
**New feature (interpretability):** Closed-form expressions computed directly from TM clauses for global feature importance, feature value-range importance and local (per-prediction) importance; plus a TM-importance-driven dimension reduction/clustering algorithm for visualization.

### Increasing the Inference and Learning Speed of Tsetlin Machines with Clause Indexing (2020)

`2020_Increasing_Inference_and_Learning_Speed_with_Clause_Indexing_arXiv2004.03188` · arXiv preprint · arXiv:2004.03188

**TM variants:** Vanilla TM, Indexed TM  
**New feature (training_speed):** Clause indexing: a look-up table indexing clauses by the literals that falsify them (inclusion lists + position matrix with constant-time updates), so clause evaluation iterates only over falsifying literals instead of all clauses, during both inference and learning.

### Low-Latency Asynchronous Logic Design for Inference at the Edge (2020)

`2020_Low_Latency_Asynchronous_Logic_Design_for_Inference_at_the_Edge_arXiv2012.03402` · arXiv preprint · arXiv:2012.03402

**TM variants:** Vanilla TM  
**New feature (hardware):** Self-timed, early-propagative dual-rail (QDI) asynchronous circuit for the TM inference datapath (clause evaluation, population count, 1-of-3 encoded magnitude comparator) with a reduced completion-detection scheme; ~10x lower average latency than synchronous at similar area and functional from 0.25-1.2 V supply.

### Massively Parallel and Asynchronous Tsetlin Machine Architecture Supporting Almost Constant-Time Scaling (2021)

`2020_Massively_Parallel_and_Asynchronous_TM_Architecture_arXiv2009.04861` · ICML 2021 (PMLR 139) · arXiv:2009.04861 · [code](https://github.com/cair/ICML-Massively-Parallel-and-Asynchronous-Tsetlin-Machine-Architecture)

**TM variants:** Vanilla TM, Regression TM, Indexed TM, CUDA asynchronous TM  
**New feature (training_speed):** Desynchronized clause evaluation: each clause runs in its own GPU thread and learns from local (possibly outdated) per-example voting tallies updated with atomic adds, removing the voting synchronization bottleneck and giving almost constant training time up to thousands of clauses.  
**Datasets:** `bike-sharing`, `blogfeedback`, `bbc-sports`, `20-newsgroups`, `semeval-2010-task8`, `imdb`, `wsd-java`, `wsd-apple`

### Coalesced Multi-Output Tsetlin Machines with Clause Sharing (2021)

`2021_Coalesced_Multi_Output_Tsetlin_Machines_with_Clause_Sharing_arXiv2108.07594` · arXiv preprint · arXiv:2108.07594 · [code](https://github.com/cair/PyCoalescedTsetlinMachineCUDA)

**TM variants:** Coalesced TM, Convolutional TM, Weighted TM, Vanilla TM  
**New feature (architecture):** Clause sharing: a single pool of clauses shared by all outputs, each clause connected to every output via a signed integer weight learned with Stochastic Searching on the Line, jointly with TA-learned clause composition (Coalesced TM, CoTM).  
**Datasets:** `noisy-2d-xor`, `mnist`, `kuzushiji-mnist`, `fashion-mnist`, `imdb-imbalanced`, `cifar-10-imbalanced`

Voting margins recorded exactly as printed, though they are inconsistent across tables (e.g. 25K vs 2.5K at 2K clauses). Discrepancies in paper: abstract attributes 71.99->89.66% (50 clauses) to Fashion-MNIST, but those numbers are in the Kuzushiji-MNIST table (Table 4); text says 98.26% for 50 clauses on MNIST while Table 2 gives 98.33. Table 5 baselines are copied from the CTM paper. Table 6 values are accuracy reductions (percentage points) vs. no removal; absolute IMDb accuracy not given. Table 7 F1 in 0-1. PDF pages could not be rendered (no poppler); text tables were clean.

### Drop Clause: Enhancing Performance, Interpretability and Robustness of the Tsetlin Machine (2021)

`2021_Drop_Clause_Performance_Interpretability_Robustness_arXiv2105.14506` · arXiv preprint (v2 Jan 2022) · arXiv:2105.14506

**TM variants:** Weighted TM, Convolutional TM, Drop Clause TM  
**New feature (algorithm):** Drop clause: each clause is switched off with probability p for a complete training epoch (dropout analogue), adding stochasticity that improves accuracy, training speed, interpretability and robustness.  
**Datasets:** `imdb`, `reuters-21578-r8`, `reuters-21578-r52`, `mr`, `trec`, `mnist`, `fashion-mnist`, `cifar-10`, `cifar-100`, `kuzushiji-mnist`, `mnist-c`, `mr-perturbed`

### Convolutional Regression Tsetlin Machine: An Interpretable Approach to Convolutional Regression (2021)

`3468891.3468901` · ICMLT 2021 (6th International Conference on Machine Learning Technologies), ACM · 10.1145/3468891.3468901

**New feature (architecture):** Convolutional Regression TM (C-RTM): combines CTM convolution (clauses as location-aware filters, OR over patches) with the RTM output layer (polarity-free clause sum normalised by T to a real value, error-proportional Type I/II feedback).

### Resilient Biomedical Systems Design Under Noise Using Logic-Based Machine Learning (2022)

`2022_Resilient_Biomedical_Systems_Design_Under_Noise_LogicML_Frontiers` · Frontiers in Control Engineering 2:778118 · 10.3389/fcteg.2021.778118

**TM variants:** Vanilla TM  
**New feature (other):** Studies TM robustness to Gaussian noise injection (SNR -15..15 dB) on medical tabular data and proposes quantile binning + Espresso logic minimisation as a noise-filtering, feature-reducing Booleanization; analyses clause Nash equilibrium via t-SNE and compares parameters/energy with binarized neural networks.

### Building Concise Logical Patterns by Constraining Tsetlin Machine Clause Size (2023)

`2023_Building_Concise_Logical_Patterns_by_Constraining_Clause_Size_arXiv2301.08190` · IJCAI 2023 (arXiv v1 preprint version) · arXiv:2301.08190

**TM variants:** Vanilla TM, Convolutional TM, Regression TM, Clause Size Constrained TM (CSC-TM), Label-Critic TM  
**New feature (interpretability):** Clause Size Constrained TM (CSC-TM): a soft literal budget b on clause size; once a clause exceeds b literals, Type I feedback only reinforces Exclude, so oversized clauses expel literals. Includes convergence analysis for XOR/OR and a hardware switching-activity argument.  
**Datasets:** `bbc-sports`, `reuters-21578-r8`, `trec`, `semeval-2010-task8`, `imdb`, `california-housing`, `cifar-2`, `mnist`, `mnist-0-1`, `energy-performance`, `hex`

### Contracting Tsetlin Machine with Absorbing Automata (2023)

`2023_Contracting_Tsetlin_Machine_with_Absorbing_Automata_arXiv2310.11481` · arXiv preprint · arXiv:2310.11481

**TM variants:** Vanilla TM, Contracting TM, Sparse TM  
**New feature (training_speed):** Absorbing Tsetlin automata: once a TA passes an absorbing Exclude (or Include) state it is removed permanently (literal discarded or fixed into the clause), using a sparse list-based clause structure so clauses contract during training, cutting training time; also discusses hardware TA circuits with absorbing states.  
**Datasets:** `trec`, `mpqa`, `cr`, `subj`, `reuters-21578-r8`, `reuters-21578-r52`

### Drop Clause: Enhancing Performance, Robustness and Pattern Recognition Capabilities of the Tsetlin Machine (2023)

`2023_Drop_Clause_AAAI_camera_ready` · AAAI 2023 (Thirty-Seventh AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence) · arXiv:2105.14506 · [code](https://github.com/Anonymous-2491/Drop-Clause-Interpretable-TM)

**TM variants:** Weighted TM, Convolutional TM, Drop Clause TM  
**New feature (algorithm):** Drop clause: each clause is switched off with probability p for a complete training epoch (dropout analogue), adding stochasticity that improves accuracy, training speed, interpretability and robustness.  
**Datasets:** `imdb`, `reuters-21578-r8`, `reuters-21578-r52`, `mr`, `trec`, `mnist`, `fashion-mnist`, `cifar-10`, `cifar-100`, `mnist-c`, `mr-perturbed`

### Generating Bayesian Network Models from Data Using Tsetlin Machines (2023)

`2023_Generating_Bayesian_Network_Models_from_Data_Using_TM_arXiv2305.10538` · arXiv preprint · arXiv:2305.10538

**TM variants:** Coalesced TM, Weighted TM  
**New feature (interpretability):** Uses TM global feature-strength indicators (clause weights x literal frequencies) obtained by training one TM per variable as target to propose parent/child candidates, then a search with lower-strength-direction pruning and cycle removal to build a Bayesian network DAG.  
**Datasets:** `bn-asia`, `bn-child`, `bn-insurance`, `bn-diabetes`, `kaggle-supply-chain-makeup`, `bank-customer-churn`

### IMBUE: In-Memory Boolean-to-CUrrent Inference ArchitecturE for Tsetlin Machines (2023)

`2023_IMBUE_In_Memory_Boolean_to_Current_Inference_Architecture_arXiv2305.12914` · ACM/IEEE ISLPED 2023 (arXiv preprint) · arXiv:2305.12914

**TM variants:** Vanilla TM  
**New feature (hardware):** In-memory TM inference on a 1T1R ReRAM crossbar: TA include/exclude actions stored as LRS/HRS, Boolean literals applied as voltages, and clause evaluation done by Kirchhoff current summation (Boolean-to-Current) over partial-clause columns of 32 TAs sensed by a 65 nm CMOS current sense amplifier, avoiding ADCs/DACs.  
**Datasets:** `noisy-xor`, `mnist`, `kuzushiji-mnist`, `fashion-mnist`, `google-speech-commands`

### TMComposites: Plug-and-Play Collaboration Between Specialized Tsetlin Machines (2023)

`2023_TMComposites_Plug_and_Play_Collaboration_Between_Specialized_TMs_arXiv2309.04801` · arXiv preprint · arXiv:2309.04801 · [code](https://github.com/cair/Plug-and-Play-Collaboration-Between-Specialized-Tsetlin-Machines)

### Tsetlin Machine Embedding: Representing Words Using Logical Expressions (2023)

`2023_TM_Embedding_TM_Autoencoder_Logical_Expressions_arXiv2301.00709` · arXiv preprint · arXiv:2301.00709 · [code](https://github.com/cair/tmu)

### Exploring Effects of Hyperdimensional Vectors for Tsetlin Machines (2024)

`2024_Effects_of_Hyperdimensional_Vectors_for_Tsetlin_Machines_arXiv2406.02648` · arXiv preprint (published at ISTM 2024) · arXiv:2406.02648

**TM variants:** Hypervector TM, Vanilla TM  
**New feature (other):** Hypervector Tsetlin Machine (HVTM): input tokens mapped to random sparse binary hypervectors combined by binding (cyclic shift) and bundling (OR), giving a fixed-size Boolean input for arbitrary structures; Reasoning by Elimination (s=1) found suited to sparse hyperspaces.  
**Datasets:** `trec`, `hiv-moleculenet`, `imdb`, `mnist`

### IMPACT: In-Memory ComPuting Architecture Based on Y-FlAsh Technology for Coalesced Tsetlin Machine Inference (2024)

`2024_IMPACT_In_Memory_Computing_Y_Flash_Coalesced_TM_Inference_arXiv2412.05327` · Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A (preprint, arXiv) · arXiv:2412.05327

**TM variants:** Coalesced TM  
**New feature (hardware):** First in-memory-computing inference architecture for the Coalesced TM built on Y-Flash memristor crossbars (180 nm CMOS): a Boolean-mode clause crossbar tile (2048x500) storing TA include/exclude as HCS/LCS with CSA-based clause sensing, and an analog-tuned class crossbar tile (500x10) storing unipolar-shifted clause weights as multi-level conductances, with pre-tune/fine-tune weight programming.  
**Datasets:** `mnist`, `iris`, `cifar-2`, `google-speech-commands`, `fashion-mnist`, `emg-gestures`, `gesture-phase-segmentation`, `human-activity`

### In-Memory Learning Automata Architecture using Y-Flash Cell (2024)

`2024_In_Memory_Learning_Automata_Architecture_using_Y_Flash_Cell_arXiv2408.09456` · IEEE conference 2024 (arXiv preprint; IEEE ISBN 979-8-3315-0498-4/24) · arXiv:2408.09456

**TM variants:** Vanilla TM  
**New feature (hardware):** Maps the full multi-state Tsetlin Automaton (not just its final action) onto the analog conductance of a single Y-Flash floating-gate memristor (180 nm CMOS), with 40 measured states (up to ~1000 with 10 us pulses), and uses an accumulating divergence counter (+-15 threshold) so the cell is only blind-written when accumulated TA state changes cross the threshold, enabling in-memory on-edge TM learning.  
**Datasets:** `xor`

| Dataset | Model | Metric | Value | Split | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `xor` | TA-on-Y-Flash mapping with divergence counter **(proposed)** | write pulses to track TA trajectories | 19 pulses | train | Sec. II-B / Fig. 5 |
| (no dataset) | Y-Flash cell (180 nm CMOS) **(proposed)** | read energy per pulse | 9.14e-06 nJ | – | Table II |
| (no dataset) | Y-Flash cell (180 nm CMOS) **(proposed)** | program energy per pulse | 139 nJ | – | Table II |
| (no dataset) | Y-Flash cell (180 nm CMOS) **(proposed)** | erase energy per pulse | 0.0016 nJ | – | Table II |

> No classification accuracy, latency or throughput is reported; the paper is a device/mapping study. Device variability (C2C over 250 cycles: LCS 0.8-0.9 nS, HCS 1-1.08 uS; D2D over 100 devices: LCS mean 0.92 nS sd 0.047 nS, HCS mean 1.04 uS sd 0.027 uS; max program/erase time 8.6/11.2 ms) is summarised here rather than as results. Device-level energy results have dataset_id null. Table II confirmed from the PDF page render.

### Pre-Sorted Tsetlin Machine (The Genetic K-Medoid Method) (2024)

`2024_Pre_Sorted_Tsetlin_Machine_Genetic_K_Medoid_arXiv2403.09680` · arXiv preprint · arXiv:2403.09680

**TM variants:** Vanilla TM, Pre-Sorted TM (K independent TMs)  
**New feature (training_speed):** A pre-sort stage before TM training: a genetic algorithm solves Hamming-distance maximum dispersion to seed binary K-medoid clustering per class, then a genetic algorithm aligns clusters across classes to maximise inter-class Hamming distance, and each aligned group trains its own smaller TM.  
**Datasets:** `fashion-mnist`, `kuzushiji-mnist`, `emnist`, `mnist`

### TPFL: Tsetlin-Personalized Federated Learning with Confidence-Based Clustering (2024)

`2024_TPFL_Tsetlin_Personalized_Federated_Learning_Confidence_Clustering_arXiv2409.10392` · arXiv preprint · arXiv:2409.10392 · [code](https://github.com/russelljeffrey/TPFL)

**TM variants:** Weighted TM, FedTM  
**New feature (privacy):** Personalized federated learning with Tsetlin machines where each client uploads only the clause-weight vector of the class it is most confident about (confidence from TM votes on a held-out confidence set); the server clusters clients per class and averages weights within each cluster, giving at most C clusters and very low communication cost.

### The Probabilistic Tsetlin Machine: A Novel Approach to Uncertainty Quantification (2024)

`2024_The_Probabilistic_Tsetlin_Machine_Uncertainty_Quantification_arXiv2410.17851` · 8th International Conference on Advances in Artificial Intelligence 2024, ACM (author version on arXiv) · arXiv:2410.17851

**TM variants:** Probabilistic TM  
**New feature (uncertainty):** Probabilistic Tsetlin Machine (PTM): instead of a single TA state, each TA keeps a probability vector over its states, updated via transition-probability matrices derived from Type I/II feedback; at inference states are sampled (BNN-like) to give predictive mean, entropy and mutual information for uncertainty quantification.  
**Datasets:** `noisy-xor`, `synthetic-2d-binary`, `iris`

PTM hyper-parameters (clauses, T, s, states) not stated except m=4 clauses and 8 states (figure axes) for noisy-XOR. Iris dataset sizes not stated (150 samples well known).

### The Sparse Tsetlin Machine: Sparse Representation with Active Literals (2024)

`2024_The_Sparse_Tsetlin_Machine_Active_Literals_arXiv2405.02375` · arXiv preprint · arXiv:2405.02375

**TM variants:** Sparse TM, Contracting TM  
**New feature (training_speed):** Sparse Tsetlin Machine (STM): clauses stored sparsely with an Active Literals (AL) list acting as a gatekeeper that introduces only literals present in current data; literals are discarded below a lower-state threshold and clause size is capped, giving constant small memory and fast training on very sparse/high-dimensional data.  
**Datasets:** `cr`, `subj`, `mpqa`, `sst-2`, `mr`, `pros-cons`, `tunadromd`, `amazon-reviews-2018`

### Event-Driven Digital-Time-Domain Inference Architectures for Tsetlin Machines (2025)

`2025_Event_Driven_Digital_Time_Domain_Inference_Architectures_for_TMs_arXiv2511.09527` · arXiv preprint · arXiv:2511.09527

**TM variants:** Vanilla TM, Coalesced TM  
**New feature (hardware):** Event-driven asynchronous (two-phase bundled-data click-element) TM inference with class-sum and argmax moved to the time domain: Hamming-distance delay accumulation plus Winner-Takes-All arbitration for multi-class TM, and differential sign/magnitude delay paths with leading-ones-detector logarithmic delay compression for the signed weights of the Coalesced TM.

### Fuzzy-Pattern Tsetlin Machine (2025)

`2025_Fuzzy_Pattern_Tsetlin_Machine_arXiv2508.08350` · arXiv preprint · arXiv:2508.08350 · [code](https://github.com/BooBSD/FuzzyPatternTM)

**TM variants:** Fuzzy Pattern TM, Coalesced TM, Weighted Coalesced TM, Vanilla TM, Graph TM  
**New feature (algorithm):** Fuzzy-Pattern TM (FPTM): clause evaluation is fuzzy - a clause votes min(#literals, LF) minus the number of failed literals (clipped at 0) instead of all-or-nothing, so each clause represents many sub-patterns; also deterministic Type Ia feedback and a clause-size cap L. Drastically fewer clauses, less memory and faster training.  
**Datasets:** `imdb`, `fashion-mnist`, `amazon-sales-noisy`

### A Novel Approach To Implementing Knowledge Distillation In Tsetlin Machines (2025)

`2025_Knowledge_Distillation_in_Tsetlin_Machines_arXiv2504.01798` · M.S. thesis, University of Cincinnati (arXiv preprint) · arXiv:2504.01798 · [code](https://github.com/ckinateder/pyTsetlinMachineParallel)

**TM variants:** Weighted TM, Multi-class Weighted TM with knowledge distillation (CKD, DKD)  
**New feature (algorithm):** Knowledge distillation for Tsetlin machines: clause-based KD (teacher clause outputs as student input, with probabilistic clause downsampling) and distribution-enhanced KD (teacher soft labels from class-sum distributions plus clause-transfer initialization of the smaller student).

### Omni TM-AE: A Scalable and Interpretable Embedding Model Using the Full Tsetlin Machine State Space (2025)

`2025_Omni_TM_AE_Full_State_Space_Embedding_arXiv2505.16386` · arXiv preprint (under review) · arXiv:2505.16386

**TM variants:** TM Autoencoder, Coalesced TM, Vanilla TM  
**New feature (architecture):** Omni TM-AE builds reusable word embeddings in a single training phase from the full TA state matrix of the TM Autoencoder, including excluded literals: each feature's embedding component is the sum of its literal states minus its negation's states over positive-weight clauses, normalised by clause count.  
**Datasets:** `one-billion-word`, `ws-353`, `mturk-287`, `mturk-771`, `rg-65`, `men`, `imdb`, `20-newsgroups`, `reuters-21578`, `yelp`, `amazon`, `ag-news`

### Scalable Bayesian Network Structure Learning Using Tsetlin Machine to Constrain the Search Space (2025)

`2025_Scalable_Bayesian_Network_Structure_Learning_TM_arXiv2511.19273` · arXiv preprint · arXiv:2511.19273

**TM variants:** Weighted TM  
**New feature (algorithm):** A parents-children BN structure learner that trains a Weighted TM per target variable, ranks variables by clause frequency x total absolute clause weight, keeps the top-2, and runs a fixed small number (~16) of CI tests per target, giving linear complexity vs PC/MB-based methods.

### A Tsetlin Machine Image Classification Accelerator on a Flexible Substrate (2025)

`2025_TM_Image_Classification_Accelerator_on_a_Flexible_Substrate_arXiv2510.15519` · arXiv preprint · arXiv:2510.15519

**TM variants:** Vanilla TM  
**New feature (hardware):** First digital TM inference engines on a flexible integrated circuit (Pragmatic 600 nm IGZO thin-film FlexIC): hard-wired 4-stage pipelined TM (clause logic, adder tree, argmax) for 8x8 handwritten digits, in a full-scale and a compact variant, with model selection over 500 random seeds to trade accuracy against gate count.  
**Datasets:** `uci-optdigits`

### The Tsetlin Machine Goes Deep: Logical Learning and Reasoning With Graphs (2025)

`2025_The_Tsetlin_Machine_Goes_Deep_Graphs_arXiv2507.14874` · arXiv preprint (v2, May 2026) · arXiv:2507.14874

**TM variants:** Graph TM, Convolutional Coalesced TM, Vanilla TM  
**New feature (architecture):** Graph Tsetlin Machine (GraphTM): learns nested deep clauses over hypervector-encoded directed, labelled multigraphs via message passing between nodes, built on the convolutional Coalesced TM; supports sequences, grids, relations and multimodal input.  
**Datasets:** `three-consecutive-a-sequences`, `mnist`, `fashion-mnist`, `cifar-10`, `mnist-superpixels`, `imdb`, `yelp-polarity`, `mpqa`, `scone-tangram`, `amazon-sales`, `movielens`, `ncbi-viral-genome`, `multivalue-noisy-xor`

### A Methodology for Transparent Logic-Based Classification Using a Multi-Task Convolutional Tsetlin Machine (2025)

`2025_Transparent_Logic_Based_Classification_Multi_Task_Convolutional_TM_RGB_arXiv2510.01906` · arXiv preprint · arXiv:2510.01906

**TM variants:** Convolutional TM, Coalesced TM, Multi-output Convolutional Coalesced TM  
**New feature (interpretability):** Interpretation methodology for convolutional (coalesced) TM clauses: local interpretations that project activated clause literals back onto the image, and global class representations built via patch counting and thermometer decoding of position literals; applied to RGB multi-label CelebA.

### TsetlinKWS: A 65nm 16.58uW, 0.63mm2 State-Driven Convolutional Tsetlin Machine-Based Accelerator For Keyword Spotting (2025)

`2025_TsetlinKWS_65nm_State_Driven_Convolutional_TM_Accelerator_arXiv2510.24282` · arXiv preprint (submitted to IEEE) · arXiv:2510.24282 · [code](https://github.com/Baizhou-713/TsetlinKWS)

**TM variants:** Convolutional TM  
**New feature (hardware):** Algorithm-hardware co-design of a Convolutional TM keyword-spotting chip: MFSC + spectral-flux Boolean features with streaming adaptive thresholds, full-spectrum (64x7) spectral convolution kernels, OG-BCSR sparse compression of TA actions via maximum-weight matching (9.84x smaller model), and a state-driven PE-array architecture exploiting both sparsity and data reuse with simulated-annealing clause scheduling.

### Uncertainty Quantification in the Tsetlin Machine (2025)

`2025_Uncertainty_Quantification_in_the_Tsetlin_Machine_arXiv2507.04175` · arXiv preprint · arXiv:2507.04175

**TM variants:** Weighted TM, Convolutional TM  
**New feature (uncertainty):** A probability score P(y=1/x)=(1+v/T)/2 derived from the Type I/II feedback equilibrium of the TM class sum, plus a normalized multiclass variant, used for uncertainty quantification and selective prediction.  
**Datasets:** `single-pattern-noise`, `three-feature-cpt`, `two-moons`, `cifar-10`

### CTM-UNet: Integrating Convolutional Tsetlin Machines with U-Net Architecture for Semantic Segmentation (2025)

`CTM-UNet_Integrating_Convolutional_Tsetlin_Machines_with_U-Net_Architecture_for_Semantic_Segmentation` · 2025 International Symposium on the Tsetlin Machine (ISTM), IEEE · 10.1109/ISTM67926.2025.00013 · [code](https://github.com/yiliu-coding/CTM-UNet/tree/master)

**TM variants:** Convolutional TM, CTM-UNet (hybrid CTM blocks in U-Net)  
**New feature (architecture):** CTM-UNet: a U-Net encoder-decoder whose convolutional blocks are replaced by (conv preprocessing + binarization + CTM2D) blocks producing integer votes cast to float, with per-class CTM heads trained by one-vs-rest Type I/II feedback; hybrid with PyTorch tensors.

### Autonomous Collaborative Learning Among an Ensemble of Tsetlin Machines with Consensus-Based Inference (2026)

`2026_Autonomous_Collaborative_Learning_Ensemble_of_TMs_Consensus_Inference_arXiv2607.20124` · arXiv preprint · arXiv:2607.20124

**TM variants:** Vanilla TM, Hierarchical two-layer TM ensemble  
**New feature (privacy):** Decentralized vertical-federated learning among an ensemble of TM agents: each agent's input-layer TM sees only its own feature tile, a second neighbourhood-aggregation TM learns from its own and neighbours' binary clause outputs, and a gossip broadcast protocol spreads vote sums to reach a network-wide consensus prediction without sharing raw data or model parameters.  
**Datasets:** `mnist`, `fashion-mnist`, `synthetic-heterogeneous-sensor-network`

### Compressed Recurrent Feedback in Tsetlin Machines: A Reproducible Boolean-FSM Study (2026)

`2026_Compressed_Recurrent_Feedback_in_TMs_Boolean_FSM_arXiv2609.06133` · arXiv preprint · arXiv:2609.06133 · [code](https://github.com/Ankitkumar1062/LBP2026_Ankit-Utkarsh)

**TM variants:** Recurrent TM, Weighted TM  
**New feature (architecture):** Fixed-width recurrent interface for the Recurrent Tsetlin Machine: 480 clause activations are XOR-folded into 48 bins, kept at two EMA timescales and thresholded to a 96-bit Boolean state fed back at the next step. Evaluated on a new reproducible Boolean finite-state-machine benchmark with ablations, raw-feedback and no-feedback controls.  
**Datasets:** `boolean-fsm-6bit`, `boolean-fsm-8bit`

### FastOmniTMAE: Parallel Clause Learning for Scalable and Hardware-Efficient Tsetlin Embeddings (2026)

`2026_FastOmniTMAE_Parallel_Clause_Learning_arXiv2605.06982` · arXiv preprint · arXiv:2605.06982

**TM variants:** TM Autoencoder, Omni TM-AE, Coalesced TM  
**New feature (training_speed):** Reformulates Omni TM-AE word-embedding training by removing the global class_sum dependency: each clause computes its update probability locally, so evaluation and update run in parallel per clause. Implemented as a reusable SoC-FPGA training accelerator IP (Zynq-7000 Zybo, Zynq UltraScale+ ZCU104) and benchmarked against CPU, OpenCL and CUDA builds.  
**Datasets:** `one-billion-word`, `imdb`, `rg-65`, `ws-353-sim`, `mturk-287`, `mturk-771`, `men`

### Target-confidence Recourse Using tSeTlin machines: TRUST (2026)

`2026_TRUST_Target_Confidence_Recourse_Probabilistic_TM_arXiv2606.18832` · arXiv preprint · arXiv:2606.18832 · [code](https://anonymous.4open.science/r/tm_counterfactual-6360/README.md)

**TM variants:** Probabilistic TM  
**New feature (interpretability):** Target-confidence counterfactual recourse: minimal input change subject to /M(x')-tau/<=eps for a user-specified confidence tau, instantiated with a Probabilistic Tsetlin Machine plus multi-objective Bayesian optimisation, with clause-level attribution explaining why counterfactuals at the same label differ in reliability.  
**Datasets:** `synthetic-2d-gaussian`, `synthetic-5d-mixed`, `iris`, `haberman-survival`

### TsetlinWiSARD: On-Chip Training of Weightless Neural Networks using Tsetlin Automata on FPGAs (2026)

`2026_TsetlinWiSARD_On_Chip_Training_Weightless_NNs_Tsetlin_Automata_arXiv2603.24186` · DAC 2026 (63rd ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference), arXiv preprint · arXiv:2603.24186 · [code](https://github.com/nsd5g13/TsetlinWiSARD)

**TM variants:** TsetlinWiSARD (TA-trained WiSARD WNN), Vanilla TM  
**New feature (hardware):** Trains WiSARD weightless neural networks with Tsetlin automata: one TA per LUT entry, iterative reward/penalty feedback on misclassification (increment true discriminator, decrement predicted) instead of one-shot memorisation. Processor-free FPGA on-chip training architecture stores TA teams in LUTRAMs with ripple-carry adders and a bitwise LFSR for feedback probability.  
**Datasets:** `mnist`, `fashion-mnist`, `kuzushiji-mnist`, `emg-gestures`, `ucihar`, `gesture-phase-segmentation`
